analysis.evidence: The battle described in the preceding verse continues here. אֵת introduces Chedorlaomer, the first of four opposing kings. The closing phrase אַרְבָּעָה מְלָכִים אֶת־הַחֲמִשָּׁה, “four kings against the five,” confirms the relationship.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: Introduces the opposing side in battle.

draft.evidence: Genesis 14:1 identifies Chedorlaomer by the title מֶלֶךְ עֵילָם, “king of Elam.”

analysis.evidence: The title מֶלֶךְ עֵילָם, “king of Elam,” immediately follows כְּדָרְלָעֹמֶר and identifies him as the first of the four kings listed in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of the king of Elam.
